generations.prompt: Create an original, production-ready detailed pixel-art animation sprite sheet for a small natural brown kestrel seen from ABOVE AND SLIGHTLY BEHIND in a bright pastoral fantasy JRPG cinematic. Transparent background. Exactly EIGHT separate complete bird sprites arranged in a strict regular 4-column by 2-row grid; generous transparent gutters around every cell, no touching cell edges. Every bird faces STRAIGHT UP the image: head toward top edge, tail toward bottom. Same individual kestrel in every cell, tawny brown back, chestnut wing feathers with darker flight-feather bars, pale nape, a small warm gray head, a real hooked beak, dark tail bands. Feathered realistic anatomy, no humanoid face, no fantasy effects, no text, no labels, no scenery, no shadows, no frame outlines. Consistent body size, body length and shoulder/body position across all cells. Pixel style: crisp finely shaded hand-placed pixel clusters, rich natural colors, warm daylight from upper left, high-detail cinematic pixel art rather than flat icons or chibi cartoons. It should look beautiful and organic at 60-80 pixels wingspan. The first SIX cells in reading order are ONE CYCLIC WINGBEAT: 1 wings raised at the start of downstroke (foreshortened), 2 wings spread in a shallow V, 3 full broad glide with both wings extended nearly horizontally, 4 wings pressing downward with feather tips swept back, 5 wings partially folded during upstroke, 6 wings returning upward toward pose1. Keep bird torso/head/tail registered and recognizable; wings grow from the same shoulders with natural primary-feather spread. Cell7 (row2,col3) is a LEFT BANK away from camera: left wing dips and foreshortens, right wing lifts and opens, body subtly rolls left, head still points up. Cell8 (row2,col4) is the matching RIGHT BANK: reverse roll, head still up. Show the dorsal/top surfaces throughout; no front-facing bird, no sideways or backwards frame. No ornamental white halo. Entire bird silhouettes must fit completely within their individual cells.

Create one original TRANSPARENT detailed pixel-art cinematic sprite sheet, arranged as EXACTLY THREE columns and TWO rows with very large empty gutters. Six separate complete isolated subjects, one per cell, never touching cell edges or each other. Use the attached sprites as strict character/clothing/vehicle reference and match their finely shaded warm daylight pixel-art quality. No scenery, ground, captions, labels, shadows, frame borders or extra people. ROW ONE is a TRUE DIRECTLY OVERHEAD BIRD'S-EYE CAMERA looking vertically down: column1 REGENT ALDRIC standing upright on the ground, brown short hair and long navy coat with restrained brass edging and brown boots; column2 his GATE GUARD standing upright, open steel cap, slate/navy practical tunic and brown boots, one spear; column3 the COMPLETE chestnut horse pulling the small wooden provision wagon covered with weathered cream canvas, brown harness, blue cloth bundle/sacks at rear, and EXACTLY ONE seated brown-clad driver at the FRONT of the wagon behind the horse. The horse is in front toward TOP of image, wagon rear toward BOTTOM. The overhead humans must be genuinely foreshortened: head/hair or helmet top and shoulders are dominant; body below shortened, boots visible close below shoulders, not full-height front sprites, not lying down flat on the ground. Aldric faces NORTH/up; guard faces NORTH/up so game can rotate it. Wagon viewed from straight above: see canvas roof, wheel footprint and horse back with one proper head, four anatomical legs mostly hidden underneath. ROW TWO: same three subjects and proportions as rowone, now viewed from a HIGH OBLIQUE REAR-THREE-QUARTER camera from the SOUTH-EAST looking toward NORTH-WEST: column1 Aldric walking/standing toward UP-LEFT, visible back/top hair/coat and natural legs; column2 same guard standing toward UP-LEFT, visible helmet top/back and spear; column3 same complete wagon/horse heading UP-LEFT with roof, rear tailgate, four wheels in correct perspective, horse in front, and ONE brown driver seen from behind. The driver is part of the complete wagon art, no driver sprite elsewhere. Vehicles may occupy more of their cells than humans, but preserve consistent human design/scale between the two rows. Treat upper/lower versions as different camera angles of the SAME people/horse/wagon, not unrelated designs. Preserve the reference's humble utility wagon, no royal carriage, no armored knight, no sword/shield, no extra horse, no duplicate driver. Pixel art with crisp clusters and rich small-scale detail, warm sun from upper-left, NO anti-aliased white halo. Aim for easily readable overhead and high-oblique sprites at native game resolution.
